newsitem.title: USA: FTC makes Time-Warner/Turner deal final.
newsitem.headline: FTC makes Time-Warner/Turner deal final.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission said Friday it had made final, without modification, a consent agreement that permits Time Warner Inc to acquire Turner Broadcasting System Inc.
The agreement was given preliminary approval by the FTC in September 1996. At the time, the FTC required a restructuring of the proposed deal.
The FTC had said it was concerned about the role of TCI Communications Inc, which owns cable companies. TCI had contractual obligations to carry Turner and was a partial owner of Time Warner.
The FTC required TCI to divest its interest in Time Warner to a separate company, or accept less than a 10 percent non-voting interst in Time Warner.
In addition, TCI, Turner and Time Warner had to cancel long-term agreements mandating carriage of Turner.

Among other things, the FTC also barred Time Warner's programming arms from discrminating against rival cable systems and required Time Warner cable companies to carry a rival to the Turner-owned CNN.
In the interim between the tenative and the final agreement, the FTC received comments from the public.
FTC Chairman Robert Pitofsky said that "all of the concerns raised were taken into account when the commission required the restructuring of the merger in September."
The final vote was 3-2. One of the dissenters was Commissoner Mary Azcuenaga.
She said the underlying theories for the decision "do not begin to satisfy the rigorous standard for merger analysis that this agency has applied for years."
She said any analysis should "take full account of the swirling forces of innovation and technological advances in this dynamic industry." She said the decision did not do so.
